title: Gain-boosted cascode OTA
description: A cascode OTA whose cascode devices are regulated by auxiliary 'booster' amplifiers (gain-boosting / regulated cascode). A booster senses the cascoded device's drain and drives the cascode gate to hold its source fixed, so the local feedback multiplies the cascode's own intrinsic gain by the booster gain: each side's output resistance becomes about $A_{v0,boost} * A_{v0,casc} * r_o$. That lifts the single-stage gain by the booster gain — often 20-40 dB — without adding a stack device or a second signal-path pole. The price is the booster's own bandwidth: it forms a pole-zero doublet that slows settling, so the closed-loop settling is estimate-grade and the sim owns sign-off. Here one booster child models the regulation gain and is applied to both the NMOS and PMOS output cascodes.

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: nominal input CM at which the operating point is evaluated

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: I_boost
params.note: booster tail current; sets the booster bandwidth (settling doublet) — spend enough to keep it faster than the main loop

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: sets the un-boosted cascode gain av0_casc

params.name: gm_id_mir
params.note: load-mirror inversion: lower gm/ID gives higher mirror ro

params.name: gm_id_bo
params.note: booster-device inversion: sets the booster gain that multiplies each cascode's ro

params.name: vgs_est_in
params.note: estimate of the input-pair vgs, used to place the tail node; retune until input-bias-consistent is green

params.name: vds_in_est
params.note: input-device vds (drain node above the tail source)

params.name: vds_cn_est
params.note: NMOS-cascode vds (output node minus the input drain)

params.name: vds_cp_est
params.note: PMOS-cascode vds magnitude (its source node minus the output)

params.name: vds_mir_est
params.note: load-mirror vds magnitude (VDD minus the PMOS-cascode source node)

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; its ro is boosted by the NMOS cascode and its booster.

doc.title: NMOS output cascode
doc.description: Regulated cascode over the input device; its intrinsic gain av0, times the booster gain, sets the NMOS-side Rout.

doc.title: PMOS output cascode
doc.description: Regulated cascode over the load mirror; its intrinsic gain av0, times the booster gain, sets the PMOS-side Rout.

doc.title: Load mirror device
doc.description: PMOS load-mirror side at half the tail current; its ro, cascoded and boosted, sets the PMOS-side output resistance.

doc.title: Gain-boost amplifier
doc.description: The regulating auxiliary amp, modelled as a single gain stage; its DC gain av0 multiplies each cascode's intrinsic gain, and its own ft (gm/2*pi*cgg) sets the settling doublet.

rows.name: Rout_n
rows.note: NMOS side: input ro boosted by the cascode gain and again by the booster gain

rows.name: Rout_p
rows.note: PMOS side: mirror ro boosted by the cascode gain and again by the booster gain

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the two regulated-cascode sides in parallel

rows.name: f_boost
rows.note: estimate: the booster's own ft, a proxy for its bandwidth; the doublet near this frequency governs settling

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the load mirror's own density referred by gm_mir/gm_in; the boosters sit outside the main signal path and add little

rows.name: vos
rows.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, mir__W, L_mir, gm_id_mir)*mir__gm/in__gm)^2)
rows.note: input-pair offset plus the load-mirror offset referred by the gm ratio

rules.note: estimate: the booster must be faster than the main loop or its doublet slows settling; sim owns the real settling
the tail-node placement uses vgs_est_in; retune it to the reported in__vgs if this trips
